fixture_contract: The sidepanel's own OAuth token makes REST POST /api/v1/tables and POST /api/v1/tables/{id}/rows with X-Organization-Id. A run-unique synthetic name is journaled atomically before the first write; positive read credit requires created=true, done=true and matching organization. Returned table and row IDs feed the Records UI requests. Finally, same-principal DELETE /api/v1/tables/{id} archives the table and its rows, repeating 503 busy responses within the configured attempt budget, and a filtered table list must show the table absent. An interrupted journal is cleanup-only and cannot earn new read credit.

review_repair.cross_attempt_recovery: Each created table carries a fixed harness marker plus a SHA-256 digest of the signed-in principal id and approved organization id in its description, alongside a run-unique synthetic name. Before any write, every hosted attempt lists this organization's tables and archives only exact name-pattern, marker, organization and custom-kind matches from previous attempts, then verifies absence. The server-side marker remains discoverable when a prior attempt's local journal path is gone. A mismatched marker is never archived. The workflow serializes all Records attempts in one group across A and B lanes with cancel-in-progress=false, so recovery cannot archive another active Records workflow's fixture.
review_repair.terminal_states: On recovery, absent no_fixture_created and archived_verified states remain terminal with no write. ownership_unverified is re-read by the exact marker: one marked fixture can be archived and verified; an unmarked collision is left untouched and becomes no_owned_fixture_found. Recovered runs never earn positive read credit from old receipts.
review_repair.invocation_guard: The write helper refuses outside GITHUB_ACTIONS=true, RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT=github-hosted and MATRX_HOSTED_ACCEPTANCE_CASE=records-readonly-admin before any API request or journal write. The workflow's Records concurrency group is the only supported destructive recovery caller.
